answer: Terrace-resident co-presence attestation. An identity is issued only after its operator is observed continuously for days by fixed sensors embedded in a physical terrace, and the sensor set rotates with the tide of foot traffic so recordings cannot be replayed. Each new identity needs a fresh, physically distinct site visit. Since one body cannot occupy two terraces at once, an attacker's marginal cost per identity is a separate verified presence, roughly the price of a site lease plus days of occupancy. A sonnet-length audit log pins each visit to its sensor readings.
